note: Comparisons are restricted to the same SEC Item; one-to-many and many-to-one matches are allowed within an Item. Evidence-supported overlapping links with one shared disclosure are consolidated; original decisions are retained in grouping.source_alignments. Other supported matched groups may share disclosures while retaining their original links; overlap alone does not require review. Auto-matched means complete original text equality after bullet/whitespace normalization, with no LLM call for that link. Mixed exact/LLM groups retain each link's method in grouping.source_alignments. AI-verified means model review plus deterministic source checks, not human verification. Unmatched means a validated verifier decision found no counterpart in the comparison's saved disclosures, not proof of filing-wide absence. Current-only unmatched disclosures are introduced_disclosure; previous-only unmatched disclosures are removed_disclosure. Unmatched decisions remain needs_review until the run completes. Invalid, unfinished or conflicting decisions remain needs_review. Scope is saved narrative disclosures, not all tables or the entire filing.

Both disclosures address the risk that failure to meet evolving industry and market needs due to rapid technological changes and shifting customer requirements may adversely impact financial results. The 2024 disclosure highlights rapid changes in technology and standards, while the 2025 disclosure explicitly lists timely identification of industry changes and adaptation as a success dependency.

Both disclosures address the risk that success depends on timely adaptation to industry changes, R&D investments, new business models, ecosystem expansion, lifecycle management, and infrastructure scaling. The 2025 text mirrors the 2024 bulleted list of requirements for success almost identically.

• launch new offerings with new business models including software, services, and cloud solutions, as well as software-, infrastructure-, or platform-as-a-service solutions;

alignments.explanation:
Both disclosures address the core risk that inaccurate demand estimation leads to supply-demand mismatches, product shortages, and excess inventory, causing financial harm.

Both disclosures cover the risks associated with overestimating demand or customer cancellations, leading to inventory write-downs, price reductions, and penalties due to non-cancellable purchase commitments.

Both disclosures describe the complexity and revenue volatility caused by frequent product transitions, including the simultaneous shipment of new and prior architectures.

Both disclosures relate to the impact of new product introductions on engineering resources and supply chain cost management, noting that delayed customer adoption or roadmap changes can impact revenue timing.

sentences.text: If our estimates of customer demand are inaccurate, as we have experienced in the past, there could be a significant mismatch between supply and demand.
This mismatch has resulted in both product shortages and excess inventory, has varied across our market platforms, and has significantly harmed our financial results.
• rapidly changing technology or customer requirements;

Product transitions are complex and can impact our revenue as we often ship both new and prior architecture products simultaneously and we and our channel partners prepare to ship and support new products.

We have experienced and may in the future experience reduced demand for current generation architectures when customers anticipate transitions, and we may be unable to sell multiple product architectures at the same time for current and future architecture transitions.

The increasing frequency and complexity of newly introduced products may result in unanticipated quality or production issues that could increase the magnitude of inventory provisions, warranty or other costs or result in product delays.

While we have managed prior product transitions and have previously sold multiple product architectures at the same time, these transitions are difficult, may impair our ability to predict demand and impact our supply mix, and we may incur additional costs.

Long manufacturing lead times and uncertain supply and component availability, combined with a failure to estimate customer demand accurately, has led and could lead to mismatches between supply and demand.

Significant mismatches between supply and demand have varied across our market platforms, resulted in both product shortages and excess inventory, significantly harmed our financial results and could reoccur.

If we overestimate demand, or if customers cancel or defer orders or choose to purchase from our competitors, we may not be able to utilize on-hand inventory or reduce purchase commitments accordingly.

We have had to reduce average selling prices, including due to our channel pricing programs, increase prices for certain of our products as a result of our suppliers' increase in prices, write down our inventory, incur cancellation penalties, and record impairments, and may have to do so in the future.
Product transitions are complex and we often ship both new and prior architecture products simultaneously as our channel partners prepare to ship and support new products.

Qualification time for new products, customers anticipating product transitions, and channel partners reducing channel inventory of prior architectures ahead of new product introductions can reduce, or create volatility in, our revenue.

We incur significant engineering development resources for new products, and changes to our product roadmap may impact our ability to develop other products or adequately manage our supply chain cost.

Customers may delay purchasing existing products as we increase the frequency of new products or may not be able to adopt our new products as fast as forecasted, both impacting the timing of our revenue and supply chain cost.

previous_disclosures.section: Risks Related to Demand, Supply and Manufacturing
previous_disclosures.summary: The company faces risks from inaccurate demand estimation, which has historically caused significant supply-demand mismatches, product shortages, and excess inventory that harmed financial results. These mismatches stem from various factors including changing product cycles, economic conditions, new use cases like generative AI and cryptocurrency mining, and the introduction of new products. Underestimating demand leads to fulfillment failures and lost revenue, while overestimating leads to inventory write-downs and penalties. The complexity is amplified by rapid product transitions, indirect sales channels, and the uncertainty of emerging technologies like AI and the Grace CPU.

current_disclosures.section: Risks Related to Demand, Supply, and Manufacturing
current_disclosures.summary: NVIDIA faces significant risks of supply-demand mismatches due to the difficulty of accurately estimating customer demand, which is influenced by complex factors including generative AI adoption, cryptocurrency mining volatility, product development cycles, and channel inventory behavior. alignments.explanation:
Both disclosures address risks from unanticipated production/quality issues leading to significant costs or inventory provisions. 2024 D024 discusses defects causing significant remediation expenses and specific costs from a 2023 data center defect. 2025 D031 highlights that 'increased frequency and complexity... could result in unanticipated quality or production issues that could increase the magnitude of inventory provisions' and cites 'gross margins... negatively impacted by inventory provisions for low-yielding Blackwell material' as a specific example of such an issue.

Both disclosures cover the risks associated with complex hardware/software offerings and reliance on partners for component supply. 2024 D024 states 'Our hardware and software product and service offerings are complex... These risks further increase when we rely on partners to supply and manufacture components... as these arrangements reduce our direct control'. 2025 D034 mirrors this with 'Our hardware and software product and service offerings are complex... risks may also increase... when we rely on partners to supply and manufacture components... as these arrangements reduce our direct control over production.'

Both disclosures specifically address the risk that AI software products relying on third-party training data and new training methods may contain unknown defects, errors, or unintended bias. 2024 D024 states 'AI software products... rely on training data that may originate from third parties and new training methods, and the resulting products may contain unknown or undetected defects and errors, or reflect unintended bias.' 2025 D035 states 'AI software products that we or our partners offer rely on training data that may originate from third parties and new training methods, and the resulting products may contain unknown or undetected defects and errors, or reflect unintended bias.'

Both disclosures state that the company remains responsible for warranty defects despite reimbursement arrangements with component providers. 2024 D024 states 'Although arrangements with component providers may contain provisions for product defect expense reimbursement, we generally remain responsible to the customer for warranty product defects'. 2025 D036 states 'Although arrangements with component providers may contain provisions for product defect expense reimbursement, we generally remain responsible to the customer for warranty product defects'.

Both disclosures address the risk that undiscovered vulnerabilities in products or services could lead to data loss, exposure to malicious software, or attack on the products. 2024 D024 states 'Undiscovered vulnerabilities in our products or services could result in loss of data or intangible property, or expose our customers to unscrupulous third parties who develop and deploy malicious software programs that could attack our products or services.' 2025 D037 states 'Undiscovered vulnerabilities in our products or services could result in loss of data or intangible property, or expose our customers to unscrupulous third parties who develop and deploy malicious software programs that could attack our products or services.'

Both disclosures discuss the consequences of defects or errors in new products/releases after commercial shipment, including loss of market acceptance, design wins, and negative impact on financial results. 2024 D024 states 'An error or defect in new products, releases or related software drivers after commencement of commercial shipments could result in failure to achieve market acceptance, loss of design wins... negatively impact our business operations, gross margin, revenue and/or financial results.' 2025 D038 states 'An error or defect in new products, releases or related software drivers after commencement of commercial shipments could result in failure to achieve market acceptance, loss of design wins... negatively impact our business operations, gross margin, revenue and/or financial results.'

Both disclosures cite the specific example of a 2023 defect in a third-party Data Center component causing adverse effects on cost/supply and resulting in a net warranty liability. 2024 D024 states 'For example, in fiscal year 2023, a defect was identified in a third-party component embedded in certain Data Center products... We recorded a net warranty liability during fiscal year 2023 primarily in connection with this defect.' 2025 D039 states 'For example, in fiscal year 2023, a defect was identified in a third-party component embedded in certain Data Center products... We recorded a net warranty liability during fiscal year 2023 primarily in connection with this defect.'

Both disclosures address the risk and significant cost of defending product liability claims, noting that even third-party supply chain issues can lead to significant defense costs and diversion of personnel. 2024 D024 states 'if a product liability claim regarding any of our products is brought against us, even if the alleged damage is due to the actions or inactions of a third party... the cost of defending the claim could be significant and would divert the efforts of our technical and management personnel'. 2025 D040 states 'if a product liability claim regarding any of our products is brought against us, even if the alleged damage is due to the actions or inactions of a third party... the cost of defending the claim could be significant and would divert the efforts of our technical and management personnel'.

Both disclosures address the risk associated with using third-party data in AI products/models. 2024 D024 states 'AI software products... rely on training data that may originate from third parties... resulting products may contain unknown or undetected defects and errors, or reflect unintended bias.' 2025 D046 states 'We have incorporated third-party data into some of our AI models... These datasets may be flawed... or contain certain biased information... compromising the integrity of our AI outputs'. While the wording differs slightly (bias vs defects), the core topic of risk from third-party data in AI models is the same specific subject. 2024 D024 also mentions 'third-party component' in the context of data center, but D046 focuses on AI models. The shared subject is third-party data inputs to AI leading to integrity/bias/defect risks.

On January 15, 2025, the USG published the "AI Diffusion" IFR in the Federal Register.

After a 120-day delayed compliance period, the IFR will, unless modified, impose a worldwide licensing requirement on all products classified under Export Control Classification Numbers, or ECCNs, 3A090.a, 4A090.a, or corresponding .z ECCNs, including all related software and technology.
Any system that incorporates one or more of the covered integrated circuits, or ICs, (including but not limited to NVIDIA DGX, HGX, and MGX systems) will be covered by the new licensing requirement.
The AI Diffusion IFR would divide the world into three tiers, relegating most countries to "Tier 2" status.
The AI Diffusion IFR would confer special benefits on select "Universal Verified End Users", or UVEU, and lesser benefits on "National Verified End Users", or NVEU.

The AI Diffusion IFR would reduce the market for U.S.-designed and manufactured computing products and services, by expressly limiting exports, reexports, and transfers of covered products to Tier 2 countries and companies in Tier 1 countries that are either headquartered in Tier 2, or have an ultimate parent headquartered in a Tier 2 country.

alignments.explanation: Both disclosures detail the specific situations and factors that may result in excess or obsolete inventory or excess product purchase commitments. The 2024 sentence lists factors like changes in business/economic/market conditions, demand decreases, obsolescence, etc. The 2025 sentence (nvda_2025_7_P029_S001) lists essentially the same factors with nearly identical wording, confirming they describe the same specific accounting estimation topic.

sentences.text: Situations that may result in excess or obsolete inventory or excess product purchase commitments include changes in business and economic conditions, changes in market conditions, sudden and significant decreases in demand for our products, inventory obsolescence because of changing technology and customer requirements, new product introductions resulting in less demand for existing products or inconsistent spikes in demand, failure to estimate customer demand properly, ordering in advance of historical lead-times, government regulations and the impact of changes in future demand, or increase in demand for competitive products, including competitive actions.
Cancellation or deferral of customer purchase orders could result in our holding excess inventory.

Situations that may result in excess or obsolete inventory or excess product purchase commitments include changes in business and economic conditions, changes in market conditions, sudden and significant decreases in demand for our products, including potential cancellation or deferral of customer purchase orders, inventory obsolescence because of changing technology and customer requirements, new product introductions resulting in less demand for existing products or inconsistent spikes in demand, failure to estimate customer demand properly, ordering in advance of historical lead-times, government regulations and the impact of changes in future demand, or increase in demand for competitive products, including competitive actions.

sentences.text: We are subject to income taxes in the U.S. and foreign jurisdictions.
Our calculation of deferred tax assets and liabilities is based on certain estimates and judgments and involves dealing with uncertainties in the application of complex tax laws.

Our estimates of deferred tax assets and liabilities may change based, in part, on added certainty or finality to an anticipated outcome, changes in accounting standards or tax laws in the U.S. or foreign jurisdictions where we operate, or changes in other facts or circumstances.
In addition, we recognize liabilities for potential U.S. and foreign income tax contingencies based on our estimate of whether, and the extent to which, additional taxes may be due.

If we determine that payment of these amounts is unnecessary or if the recorded tax liability is less than our current assessment, we may be required to recognize an income tax benefit or additional income tax expense in our financial statements accordingly.

D049 discusses Customer A and indirect customer concentration for 2024. D048 states no single direct customer exceeded 10% in 2023. While both relate to customer concentration, D048 is a specific historical negative finding for direct customers, whereas D049 is a specific positive finding for a direct customer. They are distinct points on the concentration timeline and nature (direct vs indirect/historical). D048 matches best with no direct 2025 counterpart in the current proposals that captures the 'no customer >10%' fact for a specific year other than the current year's main table. However, looking at D049 (2025), it discusses indirect customers. D048 (2025) discusses 2023 direct customers. D049 (2024) discusses 2024 direct/indirect. There is no 2025 disclosure explicitly stating 'No direct customer >10% in 2024' in the provided list. D048 is the only 2025 disclosure making a 'no customer' statement. Given D049 (2024) is the primary source for 2024 specific customer %s, and D048 (2025) is a specific historical check, they are not a perfect semantic match in terms of 'current state'. D135 matches the methodology aspect. D136 matches the results aspect. I will split the group to ensure precise topic correspondence: D140 -> D135 (method) and D140 -> D136 (results) is not allowed as separate rows for the same previous ID if we want to avoid confusion, but the instructions allow A->[X,Y]. However, D135 and D136 are distinct topics (Method vs Results). D140 combines them. I will keep the group as is because D140's topic is 'Geographic Revenue Reporting' which encompasses both method and results. The split in 2025 is just a structural change. The explanation clarifies the shared subject.
